critical_findings.finding: Deterministic fan-in is a critical-path requirement for O2, but the plan still has blocking ambiguity on patch format + merge strategy + conflict resolution. Without a fully specified, deterministic (wall-clock-independent) merge ordering algorithm and bounded conflict policy, integration outcomes can become non-reproducible or stall indefinitely under conflicts.

closure.evidence: /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/project_capsule/open_questions/6 (Q7 diff format); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/project_capsule/open_questions/8 (Q9 conflict resolution/merge strategy); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/decision_log/2 (DEC3 depends on Q7/Q9); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/milestones/2/exit_criteria (M3 requires deterministic integration identical regardless of completion order)
closure.closure_target: Before M3 (Phase 3) exit; bake deterministic ordering + conflict thresholds into canonical schemas and validator rules, then test via the M3 reproducibility exit criterion.
closure.recommended_action: Define canonical patchset schema normalization rules + a deterministic ordering key (e.g., stable lane_id + work_plan topological index) and a deterministic conflict classification/escalation spec; add an integration validator that replays merge twice under permuted lane completion orders and requires identical repo_snapshot hashes.

critical_findings.finding: The secrets policy requires detection/redaction/blocking "before any artifact is persisted", but the architecture also requires append-only event logs and pervasive artifact/workspace writes. If any tool output, patch diff, repo snapshot, or context pack contains secrets, the system can accidentally persist them (especially in append-only logs) and then cannot safely "unwrite" them.

closure.evidence: /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/project_capsule/constraints/8 (CNS9 secrets never stored); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/requirements/19 (R20 requires detection/redaction/blocking before persistence); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/governance/tool_policy/stage_policies/4 (Validate includes secrets_scan but also artifact_write)
closure.closure_target: Before any stage that writes canonical artifacts or appends to implementation_event_log.jsonl; enforce at the storage/write boundary, not as a post-hoc validator.
closure.recommended_action: Specify a write-path guard: streaming secrets scan/redaction at the Workspace Gateway / artifact-write API; event_log must record denials using redacted excerpts/hashes only; add a hard rule that raw tool stdout/stderr is never persisted unscanned (store references + redacted summaries only).

critical_findings.finding: The tool policy for the Review stage forbids artifact_write/workspace_write, but the system requires reviewers to emit findings artifacts (e.g., review_findings.json) as canonical outputs. This mismatch can either (a) block required review artifacts and break traceability/governance gates, or (b) cause ad hoc permission exceptions that weaken deterministic enforcement.

closure.evidence: /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/governance/tool_policy/stage_policies/6/restrictions/0/artifact_write (Review artifact_write=deny); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/requirements/6 (R7 requires review_findings.json in freeze bundle); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/requirements/21 (R22 requires reviewers produce findings-only artifacts)
closure.closure_target: Before M1 Phase 1 single-lane end-to-end demonstration (since it includes Review); update policy-as-data and corresponding acceptance tests.
closure.recommended_action: Adjust Review stage policy to allow writing a single findings-only artifact type (strict allowlist) via artifact_write to canonical store, while still forbidding patch/code writes; enforce by role output-type allowlist + schema validator.

critical_findings.finding: Evidence pointer objects are not consistently RFC6901-compliant as specified: decision_log evidence_pointers include extra fields (e.g., artifact_id, quote, candidate_id) not in the required structure, and at least one json_pointer is the empty string, which violates the stated rule that pointers start with '/'. This risks systematic validator failure or silent divergence from the single evidence standard.

closure.evidence: /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/requirements/9 (R10 evidence pointer structure); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/decision_log/0/evidence_pointers/0 (extra fields beyond {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note}); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/decision_log/0/evidence_pointers/1/json_pointer (empty string); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/acceptance_tests/9/pass_criteria (AT10 requires json_pointer starting with '/')
closure.closure_target: Before implementing evidence lint validators; align decision_log and all artifacts to the exact evidence pointer schema and tighten AT10 to reject nonconforming objects.
closure.recommended_action: Define a single evidence_pointer JSON Schema and require it via $ref everywhere; forbid additionalProperties; require json_pointer to match '^/' and explicitly disallow '' (root) unless separately allowed and consistently treated.

critical_findings.finding: Flaky/nondeterministic handling is required, but concrete retry budgets/backoff/quarantine thresholds remain unspecified (blocking), and the tool policy references deterministic budgets without defining them. This can yield non-deterministic behavior across runs (different retry counts/outcomes) or repeated dead-end escalation.

closure.evidence: /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/project_capsule/open_questions/9 (Q10 retry budget/backoff requirements); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/requirements/22 (R23 requires deterministic retry rules with bounded budgets); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/governance/tool_policy/stage_policies/4/restrictions/0/retry_policy ("deterministic_budgets_only" without parameters)
closure.closure_target: Before M4 freeze gating (AT23 depends on deterministic retry/escalation); encode defaults as policy-as-data with explicit numeric budgets and tie to event_log schema.
closure.recommended_action: Specify default max retries per validator per stage, fixed backoff schedule, and a deterministic flaky classifier; require event_log entries to include attempt_number and deterministic decision fields (retry/quarantine/escalate).

critical_findings.finding: The plan simultaneously (a) defaults to network=deny in all stages, and (b) has a blocking open question on how to handle dependency installation/network requirements. For many repos, builds/tests require network/package managers; without a deterministic allowlist/offline-mirror policy, implementation can deadlock or drift into ad hoc permission expansions that break reproducibility and security posture.

closure.evidence: /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/project_capsule/open_questions/10 (Q11 dependencies requiring network); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/governance/tool_policy/stage_policies/4/restrictions/0/network (Validate network=deny); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/risk_register/14 (K15 supply-chain/network risk)
closure.closure_target: Before any real-repo execution beyond toy repos; define a deterministic dependency policy and a controlled stage where network may be enabled under allowlists with lockfile enforcement.
closure.recommended_action: Add a dependency_policy artifact (allowlisted domains, package managers, lockfile rules, mirror requirements) and make it part of repo_context.json; make network opt-in with deterministic allowlists and record all network accesses for audit.

critical_findings.finding: The system requires workspace_index.json to enumerate all workspace items and to fail runs with any unindexed item, but the plan does not specify an enforcement mechanism at write time (e.g., Workspace Gateway auto-indexing or write denial if indexing is not atomic). This can create frequent integrity failures or, worse, allow unindexed shadow state that bypasses context-pack selection and audit.

closure.evidence: /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/requirements/17 (R18 indexing required; fail if any workspace item not indexed); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/architecture/options/1/components/11 (C22 workspace manager responsibilities for unified workspace_index)
closure.closure_target: Before M1 exit (workspace governance is a Phase 1 prerequisite); define atomic write+index semantics and validate with AT18.
closure.recommended_action: Specify that all workspace writes must go through a gateway that (1) writes content, (2) writes/updates workspace_index in the same transaction, or (3) rejects the write; add a periodic scanner validator as a backstop, not the primary mechanism.

critical_findings.finding: JSON Patch is mandated for canonical artifact repair, but the plan does not provide concrete forbidden/allowed JSON Pointer path rules per artifact type, nor explicit semantic invariants (e.g., immutability of IDs, monotonic histories). Relying on schema-only validation can allow logically corrupt but schema-valid repairs (e.g., rewriting requirement IDs or trace mappings) that undermine audit and determinism.

closure.evidence: /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/requirements/11 (R12 patch-only repairs); /inputs/plan_candidate/plan_package/risk_register/10/mitigation/text (K11 calls for forbidden JSON Pointer path rules per artifact type but does not define them)
closure.closure_target: Before enabling automated patcher loops (Phase 2+) and before any acceptance test asserting safe patch repair (AT12); codify per-artifact patch allowlists/denylists and semantic validators.
closure.recommended_action: For each canonical artifact schema, define a patch_policy (allowed ops + allowed pointer prefixes + immutable fields) and enforce it pre-apply; add semantic validators for invariants like stable IDs, trace link integrity, and monotonic event sequences.
